instructions: Combine the drained chickpeas and diced cucumber in a bowl.
Whisk the lemon juice and olive oil together, then fold the dressing through the chickpeas.
Add the parsley, adjust the seasoning to your taste, and serve with bread or cooked grains.
Warm the oil in a saucepan and soften the onion over a gentle heat for about 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes. Pour in the stock and simmer for about 15 minutes, until everything is soft.
Take the pan off the heat and blend with an immersion blender. Stir in the basil and season to taste.

ingredients: finely grated zest of half a lemon
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Toss the carrots with olive oil and spread them in one layer on a baking tray.
Roast for about 25 minutes, turning once, until the carrots are tender.
Stir the parsley and lemon zest into the yogurt. Spoon it onto a plate and add the warm carrots.
Warm the oil in a frying pan. Add the mushrooms and cook until their moisture has evaporated and the edges begin to brown.
Toast the bread while the mushrooms cook. Take the pan off the heat before stirring in the yogurt.
Spoon the mushrooms over the toast, scatter over the chives, and serve immediately.
Put the lentils and cucumber in a wide bowl.
Whisk the lemon juice and oil together and fold them through the lentils.
Add the mint, season to taste, and leave the salad for a few minutes before serving.
Cook the pasta according to its packet instructions. Before draining, reserve a small cup of cooking water.
Mix the olive oil, lemon zest and a splash of cooking water in the warm empty pan, away from the heat. Add the pasta and cheese.
Toss gently, adding a little more cooking water if needed. Finish with parsley and lemon juice to taste.

ingredients: 150 ml milk or a plant alternative
instructions: Mix the oats, milk, yogurt and cinnamon in a container with a lid.
Fold in the grated apple, cover, and refrigerate overnight.
Stir before serving. Add a splash of milk if you prefer a looser texture.

ingredients: finely grated zest of half a lemon
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the potatoes with the oil and rosemary and spread them on a large baking tray.
Roast for about 40 minutes, turning halfway through, until the potatoes are tender and golden.
Remove the rosemary stems, add lemon zest and parsley, and season to taste.
Warm the oil in a saucepan and soften the onion for about 5 minutes.
Add the stock and bring to a simmer, then add the peas and cook until tender.
Take the pan off the heat, add the mint and blend with an immersion blender. Adjust the consistency with a little water if needed.

ingredients: 50 g butter or a plant alternative
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C. Put the sliced apples in a small baking dish and scatter over the cinnamon.
Rub the butter into the flour, then stir in the oats. Spread the mixture over the apples.
Bake for about 30 minutes, until the fruit is soft and the topping is golden. Serve warm.
Warm the olive oil, garlic and rosemary gently in a saucepan for a few minutes without browning the garlic.
Add the beans and a splash of water. Warm through over a low heat, stirring occasionally.
Remove the rosemary stems, add the lemon juice, season to taste and serve warm.
Arrange the tomatoes, cucumber and cooked grains in a shallow bowl.
Drizzle with olive oil and gently turn the ingredients together so the tomato juices dress the grains.
Add the basil, season to taste, and leave for a few minutes before serving.
